question: A can do a piece of work in 13 days and B can do the same piece of work in 24 days. If they work together for 5 days, how much of the work will be left?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total work = LCM(13, 24) = 312 units.

Combined efficiency of A and B = 24 + 13 = 37 units/day.

Work done in 5 days = 37 × 5 = 185 units.

Work remaining = 312 − 185 = 127 units.

Fraction of work left = 127/312.

**∴ The correct answer is 127/312.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time taken by A to complete the work = 13 days

Time taken by B to complete the work = 24 days

Number of days they worked together = 5 days

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total efficiency of A and B together = 24 + 13 = 37 units/day

⇒ Work done by A and B in 5 days = 37 × 5 = 185 units

⇒ Remaining work = Total work − Work done

⇒ Remaining work = 312 − 185 = 127 units

⇒ Fraction of work left = Remaining work ÷ Total work

⇒ Fraction of work left = 127/312

**∴ The correct answer is 127/312.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Total Work Concept

Assuming total work as the Least Common Multiple (LCM) of individual completion times makes calculations integer-based and much easier than fractional addition.

Work & Efficiency

Efficiency is inversely proportional to time. A person taking more days has lower efficiency. Efficiency = Total Work ÷ Total Days.

Work Left Fraction

Fraction of work left = 1 − (Days worked × Combined 1-day work). It simply represents the ratio of the uncompleted units to the total units.

Pipes and Cisterns

Pipes and Cisterns problems use the exact same principles as Time & Work, with leaks or emptying pipes treated as having a negative efficiency.
